items.title: Cattle car experience!
items.review_text: The staff and experience is pretty much like being herded like cattle, they treat you like you’re annoying them! It does cause one to reflect on our ancestors arriving in a crowded ship in a new country, but the staff could show more empathy for those who are paying their wages!

items.title: Worth a visit
items.review_text: Use official site, worth the trip

items.title: Inspiring and dazzling statue
items.review_text: With its majestic presence in the middle of the river, this statue truly inspires freedom and peace for all people. There is an aura around this statue that attracts thousands of people from all over the world. It also commands great respect and a humanitarian salute to all those who visit it. It is one of the most popular attractions in NY. Whether by cruise or a visit to the island, you will be dazzled and amazed to finally see it in person.

items.title: Gift from the French people to the United States
items.review_text:
This symbol was created in France under the direction of Bartholdi. It is made of copper and Eiffel designed a 46 m high central pylon to support the 225 tons of the whole structure.
You get there by ferry and as you approach the statue, it appears much more imposing than what you imagine from photographs.

items.title: Always do this trip when in town. Just keeps getting better.
items.review_text: Absolutely awesome, not to be missed.  2nd time there, still wouldn't miss it. Great value for money. Fabulous to see her from the back for once. every picture you see  is front taken. Plenty time to sit back and chill at cafe or out watching the boats enter and leave Manhattan, beautiful views. Ferry staff are A1, so nice friendly & helpful. They assist disabled completely, however once on the boat, its every man for themself (lol), but everyone is so friendly and most will help and assist. Dont go without doing this and Ellis Island. 10 stars

items.title: Fab to visit!
items.review_text:
I loved our trip to the statue. The boat trip doesn't take too long but you get amazing photos from the boat.
The statue is bigger than you think.
We pre booked the tickets & had the ones where we could go up into her crown.
If you're scared of tight spaces and no quick escape don't go up, I'm fine with tight spaces but found myself trying to get fresh air on my face & was thinking 'keep cool'. 
But it was also really cool to be in the crown. You can only stay up in it for about a minute or too as it's actually tiny and everyone else behind you wants to get in there too. 
Fab day though :)

items.title: Grammer school friends (we are 70+) day trip
items.review_text: Had a wonderful afternoon. Ferry pick up and drop off was easy to use. All personnel were kind and helpful. Our day trip was perfect. Not too crowded. And the Statue is amazing to see her close up.

items.title: Statue of Liberty was the highlight – definitely book an early ferry
items.review_text:
We really enjoyed the whole Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island experience and would definitely recommend it, especially if it’s your first trip to New York.

We booked the 9:00am ferry with Statue City Cruises and I’m really glad we chose an early time. It wasn’t too busy, everything at Battery Park was easy to find, and security and boarding were really smooth with no waiting around.

The boats were clean and comfortable and you could choose whether to sit or stand wherever you wanted, which made it really easy to get good views and photos of the Statue of Liberty and Manhattan skyline on the way over.

Liberty Island was definitely the highlight for us. Seeing the Statue of Liberty up close is really impressive and the island itself is lovely to walk around. We had pedestal tickets, which were worth doing, although we would have liked to visit the crown too. Crown tickets weren’t available when we booked, so I’d definitely recommend booking those well in advance if that’s something you want to do.

We also visited the Statue of Liberty Museum and really enjoyed it. It explains the history of the statue, how it was designed and built, and added a lot to the experience.

We spent around an hour to an hour and a half on Liberty Island, which felt about right for us, before taking the ferry across to Ellis Island.

Ellis Island was interesting and the views were nice, but personally it wasn’t as much our thing. I think if you’re particularly interested in immigration history you could spend a lot of time there, but for us Liberty Island was much more memorable.

The ferries between Liberty Island, Ellis Island and Manhattan were frequent enough and we never felt stuck anywhere. If you just miss one you may have a short wait, but nothing unreasonable.

Overall, the whole experience was really well organised and easy from start to finish. Statue City Cruises did exactly what we needed them to do, and the Statue of Liberty itself absolutely lived up to expectations. I’d happily recommend the whole experience.
